frames.narration: You asked for a way to line up three things: you, the code, and the agent, the AI assistant writing it. In your words: I assume it is one way when it is actually another. This plan finds those places, with the least effort from you.

frames.title: Earlier plans
frames.narration: If you're new, four things this plan builds on. Send hands your review to an agent session that is waiting for it, the one you opened this page from; with none waiting, a headless run, the agent started on its own, can take it. A quick check asks you to predict a case the video didn't show. An explainer quotes its sources word for word. And your memory, a file in your home folder, keeps what you've watched.

frames.title: Three pictures, three gaps
frames.narration: Three things hold a picture of the code: you, the agent, and the code itself. A gap is where two disagree. You think a review sent with no session open waits for you; in this repo, a headless run takes it. The agent remembers Send trying the hand-off to a waiting session once; it tries again fifteen seconds later. And you asked for a review that reaches the agent. The agent read any agent; you meant your open session.

frames.title: Today, and what changes
frames.narration: Today reelplanner explains one way, from the agent to you. Its checks test whether you followed the video, not what you assumed that it never said. The plan has five steps, each one change. Steps one and two: a few cards where a gap is likely. Step three: your own words, checked. Step four: one click settles each gap. Step five: the cards before a plan, and on every quick check.

frames.title: What your review changed
frames.narration: Your review changed three things. One: you can answer the agent's questions three ways, in the chat with the agent alone, on this page, or in a video. Two: something you got right is asked once more, days later, on a new case. Three: you got three of this video's quick checks wrong, so what they test is now said plainly. Those were gaps too, between the video and you.

frames.title: Step 1 · Three kinds of card
frames.narration: Step one. A round is a short set of cards, at most six, about one topic: about two minutes. A card is one of three kinds. A predict card asks what the code does, and holds the answer with the code's own lines. An assume card says what the agent assumes you want, for you to answer. A say card asks you to explain it in your own words: that's step three.

frames.title: Step 1 · Where gaps are likely
frames.narration: Picking the cards is the point. Each must say why you might picture it otherwise, and what depends on it. The agent looks at what your words take for granted, quick checks you got wrong, commits since you last watched, and its own assumptions, and keeps at most six. Then a fresh checker, an agent that never saw this conversation, answers each predict card from the code alone. Where it disagrees, the card is fixed or dropped before the round opens. You never see two answers side by side.

frames.title: Step 2 · One round, three ways in
frames.narration: Step two, as you decided: one round, three ways in. First, in the chat with the agent alone: it asks each card with its own question tool, and shows the code's lines as text. That needs no page, no video, and no setup in the repo. Then the review page, which adds clicking a box on a diagram, and your voice. Then a video, where a quick check is a card. Each way writes the same record, so what comes next is the same. Drawing your picture comes later, on the page, as a plan of its own.

frames.title: Step 2 · Predict, then see the code
frames.narration: On the review page, a card at a time, you answer first, with a letter key, or N for not sure. Then the card turns over: the file, the lines, one sentence why. Here, this repo's config sets a headless command, so a run starts. A match brings the next card. A wrong answer is a gap, with four ways to settle it. Not sure is kept too, never skipped: it's a gap of its own, settled with Got it or Show me more.

plan.problem:
The owner asked (issue #57): "basiclaly what i need here is a way to align me and the actual code + agent writing it. oftentimes we are not aligned, i assume it is one way when it is actually another. we want to actually interact to be able to do this." And: "rn reelplanner focuses on making the plans easier to understand and lowest friction. but we want to also make it easy for human to really make sure htey are aligned and interact in a way that is least effort for them to do interactions (this is what the drawing and voice was for) just like video is easiest way for them to understand."

Three things hold a picture of the code: you, the agent, and the code itself. They drift apart in three ways:

- **You and the code.** You think a review you send with no session open waits in the inbox for you. In this repo it doesn't: `.reelplanner/config.json` sets a headless command, so a headless run starts on it. Nothing told you otherwise, because nothing asked.
- **The agent and the code.** The agent read the inbox code an hour ago and remembers Send as trying once and giving up. It tries again: when the waiting session goes away, Send checks again 15 seconds later. A plan built on the agent's picture is wrong before you see it.
- **You and the agent.** You asked for "a review that reaches the agent". The agent took that to mean any agent, a headless one included. You meant the session you have open. Neither of you said so.

reelplanner today explains in one direction, from the agent to you. A plan video's quick checks test whether you followed what the video said, on a new case. They don't find what you assumed and the video never mentioned, and that is where surprises come from. The decision questions cover only the choices the agent saw. Ask about this answers what you think to ask.

Issue #53 asked for a whole-repo quiz with scores, readiness thresholds and spaced retests. That treats a wrong answer as you failing. Here a wrong answer is a finding: one of the three pictures is wrong, and it is not always yours. #53 is closed in favour of #57. Drawing your picture first (#23) stays separate for now; this plan leaves room for it as another way to give your picture.

The plan makes four changes:

1. **A round**: a few cards the agent writes where a gap is likely and costly, each about the code checked against the code, or about what you want (steps 1 and 2).
2. **Your own words**: say or type how you think it works, and each thing you said comes back checked (step 3).
3. **Settling and keeping**: one click on each gap, and what it settled goes to the right place: your memory, the plan, a fix, or a short video (step 4).
4. **Into the loop**: a round before a plan when one is worth it, the same settling on every quick check, and a count of whether it helps (step 5).

Steps 1 and 2 go together. Step 3 needs step 2. Step 4 needs step 2. Step 5 needs steps 1 and 4.

### What your review changed

You asked for changes (`reviews/plan-20261118T223944Z.md`). Three of them reshape the plan:

- **One round, three ways to answer it (step 2, D-314).** You said: "we should support multiple modalities here, but same backend for doing the review", and "an easier implementation of just doing in agent alone without video, just with something like askuserquestions or wahtever the harness suppports. then, we can do in html, and also here in video. jic some dont use full reelplanner pipelien". So a round is one record with one set of commands, and it can be answered three ways: in the chat with your agent, on the review page, or as quick checks in a video. The chat comes first: it is the easiest to build and needs no page, no video and no `reel init`.
- **A card you got comes back once more (step 4, D-316).** After Got it, the same thing is asked once more on a new case a few days later, and again whenever its lines change.
- **Three quick checks you got wrong (steps 1, 2 and 3).** The checker, Not sure, and a "should" claim are now each said plainly where they are explained. That they were missed is itself what this plan is for: three gaps between what the video said and what you took from it.

Questions 2 and 4 kept the recommendations (D-315, D-317).

### Step 1 — A round of cards, written where a gap is likely and costly

**It lets you:** get a handful of questions about exactly the places you and the agent are most likely to disagree, each one checked against the code before you see it.

This step stands alone. A **round** is a short set of **cards**, at most six, about one topic: a part of the code, a plan about to be written, a change. It takes about two minutes. `reelplanner align "<topic, in your words>" <source> …` starts one in `.reelplanner/align/<date>-<slug>/`, with `align.md` (your words, then the cards) and `sources.json`, pinned the way an explainer pins its sources: each file by its commit and fingerprint, so a card can quote it word for word.

A card is one of three kinds:

- **Predict**, about the code as it is. "In this repo, you press Send and no session is waiting. What happens to the review?" Two to four options; the page always adds **Not sure**. The card holds the right answer, the lines that show it (`scripts/lib/inbox.mjs:700-705`), those lines quoted word for word, and one sentence why.
- **Assume**, about what you want. "I'm assuming you mean the session you have open, not a headless one." It has no right answer; only you can settle it. You answer Right, Not quite (and say what), or Doesn't matter.
- **Say**, your own words: "Say how you think a review reaches the agent." Step 3.

**Choosing the cards is the point.** A round that tests what you already know wastes your time; a round of trivia is #53 again. So every card carries two lines the agent must write: `likely_wrong:`, why a reasonable person would picture it otherwise (in a repo with no headless command the review does wait, and this one has one), and `matters:`, what depends on it (step 2 of the plan; an agent you didn't expect working on your review). `align` hands the agent four places to look for candidates, and the agent picks the likeliest and costliest:

- **Your words**: what your request takes for granted. "A review that reaches the agent" takes for granted which agent.
- **Your memory**: quick checks you missed on these parts, words you looked up, answers in your own words (`reel memory --you`).
- **What moved**: commits on the pinned files since you last watched a video of these parts.
- **The agent's own assumptions**: what it would have to take for granted to write the plan. These become assume cards.

**The agent's picture is checked too.** A card with a wrong answer would teach you something false. So before you see the predict cards, a fresh agent that never saw this conversation answers each one from the pinned sources alone. Where its answer differs from the card's, the agent's picture is the wrong one: the card is fixed against the code, or dropped. **You never see two answers side by side**, and never a card with a note saying the checker disagreed: a disagreement is settled before the round opens. Who decides, and how: the agent rewrites the card once from the quoted lines, and the checker answers it again. A card reaches you only when the two agree, each reading the quoted lines on its own; neither simply wins, and the checker can misread too, which is why a card that still splits them is dropped rather than shown, and why the lines are on every card for you to read. If they still disagree, the card is dropped and listed at the end of the round as "the agent and the checker read this code differently": a gap between the agent and the code, shown to you, not hidden. The assume cards need no check and come first, so the check runs while you answer them. What a round costs before you see it: the agent's own minute or two to list candidates and write the cards, and one fresh agent reading only the cards and their pinned lines, a few thousand tokens. Step 5 counts it with the rest, so a round's cost can be weighed against the gaps it found.

`align --check` holds a round to its rules before it opens: each quote is in its source word for word (the explainer's `check-sources`), each card has `likely_wrong:` and `matters:`, there are at most six, an assume card has no answer, and no card asks what your memory says you already know, at the same fingerprint.

#### Cases

| Case | Input | What happens | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before a plan | "make Send reach my open session" | Two assume cards, three predict cards on the inbox | you ask: plan; agent lists: candidates; picked: 5 cards; checked: by a fresh agent; you see: the round |
| On its own | `reelplanner align "how a review reaches the agent" scripts/lib/inbox.mjs` | Four predict cards, one say card | you run: align; pinned: inbox.mjs; written: 5 cards; checked: quotes; you see: the round |
| The agent was wrong | A card says Send tries once; the checker reads a second try 15 s later | The card is fixed before you see it | written: card c4; checker answers: tries again; fixed: c4 against the code; you see: the right c4 |
| You know it already | Your memory knows c2 at the same fingerprint | c2 is not asked | listed: c2; memory: known at fingerprint 4b1e; dropped: c2; you see: 4 cards |
| Nothing worth asking | The agent finds no likely, costly gap | No round; the plan says so in a line | agent lists: candidates; none: likely and costly; you see: the plan |

#### Interface

```text
reelplanner align "<topic>" <source> …        # start a round: .reelplanner/align/<date>-<slug>/
  --plan <plan-dir>                          # a round before that plan; its answers go into it
reelplanner align <align-dir> --check         # quotes, likely_wrong, matters, at most six, not known already
reelplanner align <align-dir> --prompt checker  # the fresh agent's exact prompt: answer each predict card from the sources
align.md                                      # your words, then the cards, then (after) what each settled
  ### c1 · predict | assume | say             # one card
  - question:                                 # what you are asked
  - option_a: … option_d:                     # predict only; Not sure is added by the page
  - answer: <letter>                          # predict only
  - source: <path>:<from>-<to>                # predict only, a pinned source
  - quote: "<the lines, word for word>"       # predict only
  - why:                                      # one sentence, shown after you answer
  - likely_wrong:                             # why a reasonable person would picture it otherwise
  - matters:                                  # what depends on it
sources.json                                  # as an explainer's: each source pinned by commit and fingerprint
```

#### Example

You ask for a plan: "make Send reach my open session". Before writing it, the agent lists its candidates and writes five cards. c1, assume: "I'm assuming you mean the session you have open, not a headless run" (`likely_wrong:` your words say "the agent"; `matters:` step 2 of the plan). c3, predict: "In this repo, you press Send and no session is waiting. What happens to the review?" A · it waits in the inbox for the next session, B · a headless run starts on it, C · it is lost. Answer B, from `scripts/lib/inbox.mjs:700-705` and the `agent.command` in `.reelplanner/config.json`. The fresh checker answers B too, so c3 stays. c4 said Send tries once; the checker read the second try 15 seconds later, so c4 is fixed. Your memory knows c5 already, so the round has four cards.

```diagram
flow: How a round is written
your words -> candidates: what they take for granted
your memory --> candidates: missed checks, words looked up
what moved --> candidates: commits since you watched
agent's assumptions -> candidates: assume cards
candidates -> round (at most six): likely and costly | each card says why you might picture it otherwise, and what depends on it
round (at most six) -> fresh checker: predict cards
fresh checker -x round (at most six): a card the code does not back | fixed or dropped before you see it
```

### Step 2 — One round, three ways to answer it: in the chat, on the page, in a video

**It lets you:** answer a round wherever you already are, in the agent's chat, on the review page or inside a video, and get the same result each way.

Needs step 1's cards. Decided by you as D-314: the round is one **backend** (the record, the checks and where each answer goes) and several ways in. Each way asks the same cards and writes the same answers; it only adjusts how you answer, to what it can do.

**What stays the same everywhere:** the round's folder and `align.md` (step 1), the order (assume cards first, while the checker reads the predict cards), committing to an answer before seeing the code's, and one record of the answers, written by one command, `reelplanner align record <align-dir> <answers.json>`, whichever way they came. Steps 3 and 4 read only that record.

**The three ways in, in the order they are built:**

1. **In the chat, with the agent alone.** No page, no video. The agent asks each card with the harness's own question tool where it has one (`AskUserQuestion` in Claude Code), or as a plain numbered question where it doesn't. You pick, or say Not sure, or write your own words. Then it shows the card's back as text: the file and lines in a code block, the one sentence why. A gap is a second question: Got it, Change the plan, The code is wrong, Show me more. This works in a repo with no `.reelplanner/`: the round is kept in this machine's `~/.reelplanner/align/<repo-key>/`, as a quick video's inbox is, and nothing is written into the repo. This is the one to build first: it needs only the agent. In the chat, a say card is typed (or spoken through the harness's own dictation where it has one), and the session you are talking to is the one that checks it; Show me more answers at once with a longer explanation in text, and the round's one short video, when you asked for it, is built after the round and linked in the chat.
2. **On the review page.** One card at a time, a key per answer, and the card turns over to show the code's lines. Here you can also point (a card whose options are the boxes of a diagram: you click **inbox**) and speak (step 3). **Send** files the round through the inbox as a review is filed, and the waiting session's `--wait` prints it; with no session waiting it stays there, and a round never starts a headless run, as a question asked on the page never does.
3. **In a video.** A quick check is a predict card inside a video, and settles the same way (step 5).

What each way adjusts: the chat has no pointing (a diagram card is asked as its boxes' names) and no voice; the page adds pointing and voice, and later drawing your picture (#23) can come in there, since a drawing needs a page; a video asks only predict cards. On every way:

- **Same picture**: said in a line, and the next card.
- **A gap**: the four ways to settle it (step 4). Nothing goes on until you pick one.
- **Not sure**: kept, never skipped: it is a gap too, of its own kind, because you had no picture of your own. It settles two ways, Got it or Show me more, and the next card comes after.
- **Skip the rest**: ends the round; the cards you skipped go into the plan as **Assumed, not checked**, each in a line.

#### Cases

| Case | Input | What happens | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|

#### Example

In the chat, in a repo with no `.reelplanner/`, you ask: "align me on how a review reaches the agent before you change it". The agent writes four cards and asks c1 with its question tool: "I'm assuming you mean the session you have open, not a headless run. Right?" You pick Not quite, and say "only my open session". It asks c3: A · it waits for the next session, B · a headless run starts, C · it is lost. You pick A. It shows lines 700 to 702 of `scripts/lib/inbox.mjs` in a code block, and "A headless command is set here, so a review no session picks up starts a headless run." Then: Got it, Change the plan, The code is wrong, Show me more? You pick Got it. `reelplanner align record` writes both answers, and the same round could have been answered on the page instead, card c3 turning over to the same lines.

#### Look

The review page's own look, so a round feels like a part of reviewing, not a new tool: paper `#FAF9F5` and tile `#EFE9DE`, ink `#141413`, and the one coral `#B8552E` only on what is yours (your pick, the settle row while it waits on you). The question in EB Garamond at 44 px, the options and the why in Inter at 22 px, the quoted lines in JetBrains Mono at 20 px on the navy slab `#181715`, as code shows itself everywhere in reelplanner. The one thing that makes it recognisable: the card turns over, front to back, the question on one side and the code's lines on the other, so "you said, the code says" is always one card.

```diagram
flow: One round, three ways in
round (align.md) -> the chat: the agent's question tool | built first; needs no page, no video, no reel init
round (align.md) -> the page: keys, pointing, voice
round (align.md) -> a video: quick checks
the chat -> one record: align record
the page -> one record: Send
a video -> one record: the review
one record -> steps 3 and 4: the same record each way
```

### Step 3 — Say it in your own words, and see each thing you said checked

**It lets you:** talk through how you think it works for half a minute, and see your own words marked where they match the code and where they don't.

Needs step 2. On the page you can speak; in the chat you type, or use the harness's own dictation where it has one. A say card asks you to explain, not to pick: "Say how you think a review reaches the agent." Hold Space, or press the microphone, and talk. By default the page records on your machine and the local whisper the narration already uses writes your words down when you stop, in a few seconds. A browser's own live recognition shows the words as you speak, but some browsers send the audio to their maker's servers to do it, so it is off until you turn it on, and the switch says so. You can type instead, or fix a word: your words are shown before anything is checked, and nothing is checked until you press **Check**, so a word whisper misheard is fixed first, never marked as a gap. Where there is no microphone, or on a hosted page (which has no local whisper and no session to hand words to), the say card takes typed words only, and says so; where whisper is not installed and live recognition is off, it offers typing and says how to install whisper (`reelplanner setup --local-voice`). The recording stays in the inbox and is never committed; only your words go into `align.md`.

Your words go to the waiting agent session the way a question from Ask about this does: saved first, then handed to a session that is waiting or connected. The agent splits them into **claims**, each one a stretch of your own words that says one thing about the code ("it starts the agent right away"), and checks each against the pinned sources. The page shows your words with each claim marked:

- **✓ matches**, with the lines that back it. The session that marks the claims is the same agent whose picture may be wrong, so each claim it marks is then read by the fresh checker from the quoted lines alone, as a predict card is (step 1), before you see the marks; a claim the two read differently is shown as "not settled", not as a match or a gap;
- **✗ differs**: a gap, made into a card from your own words and the code's lines, settled as in step 4;
- **? the code can't say** (asked next in this same round, and not counted in its six: the limit is on the cards the agent writes, so a full round can become seven): a claim about what you want, not what is. A claim with "should", "I want" or "it'd be better if" is about what should be, so it is **neither a match nor a gap**: the code can only say what is. It becomes an assume card for you to confirm ("I'm assuming you want it to go only to your open session. Right?").

With no session waiting, your words stay with the round in the inbox, and the next session that takes the round checks them; you see them marked when it hands the round back. A say card never starts a headless run, even in a repo that sets a headless command: like a question asked on the page, it waits for a session. In the chat there is always one: the session you are answering is the one that checks your words. So a say card is checked by a session, or not yet; never by a headless run. Until one takes it, the page says "waiting for a session to check your words".

Claims are the shared format: a drawing of your picture (#23) can later produce the same claims, checked the same way.

#### Cases

| Case | Input | What happens | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mostly right | 20 s of speech, 3 claims, 2 match | Two ✓, one ✗ made into a card | you say: 3 things; split: 3 claims; checked: against inbox.mjs; you see: 2 ✓, 1 gap card |
| A want, not a fact | "and it should only go to my session" | A ? claim, as an assume card | you say: should; marked: ?; made: assume card; you answer: Right |
| The default, local | Live recognition off | Recorded, written down by local whisper when you stop | you hold: Space; recorded: 21 s; transcribed: whisper, on this machine; you see: your words |
| Live words, turned on | You switch on the browser's recognition | Words as you speak; the switch says where the audio goes | you turn on: live; you speak: words appear; kept: your words, not the audio |
| No session waiting | Nobody to check | Kept, checked after Send | you say: words; saved: inbox; you see: checked when a session takes the round |

#### Interface

```text
say card                                     # "Say how you think <topic> works"; hold Space or the mic, or type
POST /api/align/say                          # your words, saved under inbox/questions/ before any hand-off
POST /api/align/transcribe                   # a recording, through local whisper, when the browser has no recognition
reelplanner align answer <align-dir> <card> <claims.json>   # the agent's checked claims; the page shows them in seconds
claims.json                                  # [{ words, from, to, verdict: match | differs | open, source, quote }]
  from, to                                   # where in your words the claim is, so the page can mark it
```

#### Example

You hold Space and say: "When I press Send it goes to my session. If I'm not there, it waits for me. A question I ask on the page does the same." Three claims. "It goes to my session": ✓, when a session is waiting (`inbox.mjs:673`). "If I'm not there, it waits": ✗, in this repo a headless run starts, because `config.json` sets `agent.command` (`inbox.mjs:700-705`). "A question does the same": ✓, a question waits and never starts a run (the `!question` on line 700). One gap card appears under your words, with your sentence on its front and the code's lines on its back.

```diagram
flow: Your words, checked
you speak -> your words: browser recognition or whisper
your words -> waiting session: saved first, then handed on
waiting session -> claims: one stretch of your words each
claims -> ✓ matches: the lines that back it
claims -> ✗ differs: a gap card from your words
claims --> ? open: a want, not a fact | becomes an assume card
```

### Step 4 — Settle each gap, and keep what it settled where it belongs

**It lets you:** close a gap in one click and know it won't come back to bite you, in this plan or a later one.

Needs step 2. A gap is settled one of four ways, each with somewhere to go:

- **Got it**: the code is right and you had it wrong. It goes to your memory (`~/.reelplanner/you.jsonl`) as something you know: the card's claim, its file and lines, and their fingerprint. A later video drops the explanation, the way it already drops a word you know. Decided by you as D-316, it is **asked once more**: the next round on that part, three days or more after you pressed Got it, asks it again on a new case (other names, other numbers, the same rule), never the same card, so you apply what you learned instead of recalling the answer. Got it there too, and it is known for good; wrong again, and it stays a gap to settle. Nothing reminds you on a schedule: the first round in this repo three days or more later, whatever it is about, carries the due card as one more card, so a card you got does come back even when nothing touches that part again; and when a plan starts with cards due and no round is needed, the agent asks them alone, in the chat, a minute at most. If neither ever happens, the card stays due, and `reel memory --you` lists it as due until it is asked. And when those lines change, the fingerprint no longer matches and it counts as not known again, whatever came before. The fingerprint is of the lines' text, not their numbers: when an edit above them moves them, or the file is renamed, the next round finds the same text (in the file, then in the repo) and updates where it is; only when the text itself is gone or changed is it not known, and then the next round that touches it may ask it again, as a new card, never the old one.
- **Change the plan**: you want it your way. Before a plan, it goes into the plan under **You told me first**: the plan is written on it, and its video doesn't ask it again. With no plan, the round's Finish offers **Plan this**, which starts one from the round, as an explainer does; until then your words wait in `align.md` under You told me first, and the plan started from it carries them.
- **The code is wrong**: a fix, never a change made on the spot. Before a plan, it becomes a step of that plan, with the card's lines as its case. With no plan, the round's Finish drafts an issue's text, `align/<slug>/issue.md`, for you to file or to start a plan from. Nothing leaves the machine without you.
- **Show me more**: at once, the card opens a longer explanation and a diagram, from the same pinned lines. At the end of the round, the gaps you asked more on become one short explainer video, built by `reelplanner explain` from the round's sources, which starts from your picture: "You expected the review to wait for you. Here is why a headless run took it." One video for the round, not one a gap: a video takes minutes, a card seconds. It is built in the background at low depth, a few minutes and the tokens of one short video, while you go on, and the plan does not wait for it; the review page says when it is ready, as it does for a rebuilt video.

An assume card answered **Not quite** is a gap about what you want; your words go into the plan as **You told me first**. A card answered **Right** is said in the plan in one line.

**Nothing from a round goes into the decision log.** Only an answer to a plan's question is a decision, and a round is not a plan. What you settle reaches the log through the plan it shapes, as an explainer's comments do. `align.md` keeps the whole record: each card, your answer, same or a gap, and how it was settled. It is committed like an explainer's folder; a recording is never committed.

#### Cases

| Case | Input | What happens | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| Got it | c3, you had A | Known in your memory at its fingerprint, due once more | you press: Got it; kept: you.jsonl, inbox.mjs:700-705 at 4b1e; due: a new case after 3 days |
| Asked once more | A round on the inbox five days later | A new case on the same rule, not c3 again | round: on the inbox; due: c3's rule; asked: a repo with no headless command, what happens?; you pick: it waits; kept: known for good |
| The code changes | Lines 700–705 edited a week later | Not known any more | edited: inbox.mjs; fingerprint: 9c07, not 4b1e; next round: may ask again |
| Change the plan | c1, "Not quite: only my open session" | Into the plan, You told me first | you answer: Not quite; written: plan.md, You told me first; plan video: no question on it |
| The code is wrong | A card's lines do what it says, and you say no code should do that | A step of the next plan, or an issue's text | you press: The code is wrong; drafted: a step; you see: it in the plan |
| Show me more, three gaps | c2, c3, c5 | One explainer at the end of the round | you press: Show me more ×3; made: one explainer; it starts: from what you expected |

#### Interface

```text
Got it                    # you.jsonl: { knows: <claim>, repo, source: path:from-to, fingerprint, due: <date>, asked: 1 }
once more                 # the next round on that part from `due` on asks a new case on the same rule; then known for good
Change the plan           # plan.md, ## You told me first: your words, the card, the code's lines
The code is wrong         # a step of the next plan, or align/<slug>/issue.md for you to file
Show me more              # now: the card's longer page; at the end: one explainer of these gaps
Finish                    # Done · Plan this · Explain the gaps (when any asked for more)
align.md, after           # each card: your answer, same | gap | not sure, how settled
reel memory --you         # lists what you know, by repo, and lets you remove a line
```

#### Example

Of four cards you settle three gaps. c1, "Not quite: only my open session", goes into the plan's You told me first. c3 you had wrong: Got it, kept at fingerprint 4b1e and due once more in three days, on a new case. c4 you asked more on: the card opens the inbox's hand-off order as a diagram (a waiting session, then a connected one, then the headless run, then the inbox), and at Finish, Explain the gaps builds a two-minute explainer that opens with "You expected Send to try once". The plan that follows is written on c1, its video skips what c3 taught you, and nothing went into the decision log.

```diagram
flow: Where a gap goes
gap -> your memory: Got it | asked once more on a new case days later; then known until the lines change
gap -> the plan: Change the plan | You told me first
gap -> a fix: The code is wrong | a step, or an issue's text
gap -> an explainer: Show me more | one video for the round's gaps
gap -x decision log: never directly
```

### Step 5 — Into the loop: before a plan, in every quick check, and measured

**It lets you:** get a round only when one is worth your time, settle a wrong quick check the same way, and see whether rounds make later surprises rarer.

Needs steps 1 and 4.

**Before a plan.** When you ask for a plan on code that exists, the skill lists gap candidates first (step 1's four places). A candidate is **likely** when one of the four places points at it: your words take it for granted, you missed a check on that part, it changed since you last watched, or it is an assumption the agent can't check alone. It is **costly** when a step of the plan depends on it, or it is hard to undo (stored data and formats, permissions, what other people's code relies on: the walkthrough's own label). You can always ask for one, "align me first", whatever the agent judged. When one is likely and costly, it runs a round before writing the plan, with `--plan` so the answers go into it. The plan then starts from where you stand: what you settled is said in a line, what you knew is not explained again.

**A new project.** With no code yet there is nothing to predict, so a round before a plan in a new project holds only assume and say cards: what the agent assumes you want, and how you picture what you are asking for.

**Every quick check settles like a card.** A quick check is a predict card inside a video. In a plan video, nothing is built yet, so its quick check asks what the plan will do, and settles three ways: Got it (you had the plan wrong), Change the plan, Show me more. A walkthrough's and the system video's quick checks are about code that exists, and add The code is wrong. Today a wrong answer shows Walk me through it and the box "Expected something else?". With this, a wrong answer also offers the same four ways: Got it (into your memory), Change the plan and The code is wrong (each with your words, reaching the agent as a comment does now), Show me more (Walk me through it). The box's words become Change the plan's words, so nothing you can do now is lost. A wrong quick check left unsettled is recorded as it is today, and never blocks Approve.

**Measured.** `reel status` gains a memory line: rounds, gaps found per round, and how they were settled. And it compares later surprises (answers in your own words, "Expected something else", choices you flagged in a walkthrough, late fixes) on plans that had a round with plans that didn't. It reports the counts and says nothing about whether rounds help until five plans of each kind exist. "Each way" means plans that had a round and plans where the agent found a likely, costly gap but no round ran. To compare like with like, the plans without a round it counts are the ones where the agent found a likely, costly gap and no round ran (you skipped it, or rounds were off), not the easy ones where it found none. It prints, for example, `late fixes · with a round 1 · likely gap, no round 4`, and below five plans of each, `too few plans to compare`.

#### Cases

| Case | Input | What happens | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| A plan with a likely gap | "make Send reach my open session" | A round of four, then the plan | you ask: plan; candidates: 6; likely and costly: 4; you see: a round, then the plan |
| A plan with none | "rename the Save button" | No round | you ask: plan; candidates: 1, not costly; you see: the plan |
| A wrong quick check | k2, you picked A | The four ways under the answer | you pick: A; you see: B marked, the four ways; you press: Got it; kept: you.jsonl |
| Too early to say | 3 plans with a round, 2 without | Counts only | you run: reel status; you see: 3 rounds, 11 gaps, 7 Got it; "too few plans to compare" |

#### Interface

```text
the plan-to-video skill, A new plan   # lists candidates; runs a round when one is likely and costly
plan.md, ## You told me first         # what the round settled, each with its card
quick check, a wrong answer           # Got it · Change the plan · The code is wrong · Show me more
reel status                           # rounds: 3, gaps: 11 (Got it 7, the plan 3, a fix 1); compared after 5 and 5
```

#### Example

You ask for a plan to make Send reach your open session. The agent finds six candidates, four likely and costly, and opens a round of four. You settle two gaps. The plan is written with "You told me first: only the session you have open". In its video, quick check k2 asks what happens when two sessions are open; you pick A, the wrong one, and press Got it. Three weeks later `reel status` says 3 rounds, 11 gaps, and "too few plans to compare".

```diagram
flow: Before a plan
your request -> candidates: step 1's four places
candidates -> a round: one likely and costly
candidates --> the plan: none worth asking | no round
a round -> the plan: You told me first
the plan -> its video: skips what you knew
```

steps.title: A round of cards, written where a gap is likely and costly
steps.text:
**It lets you:** get a handful of questions about exactly the places you and the agent are most likely to disagree, each one checked against the code before you see it.

This step stands alone. A **round** is a short set of **cards**, at most six, about one topic: a part of the code, a plan about to be written, a change. It takes about two minutes. `reelplanner align "<topic, in your words>" <source> …` starts one in `.reelplanner/align/<date>-<slug>/`, with `align.md` (your words, then the cards) and `sources.json`, pinned the way an explainer pins its sources: each file by its commit and fingerprint, so a card can quote it word for word.

A card is one of three kinds:

- **Predict**, about the code as it is. "In this repo, you press Send and no session is waiting. What happens to the review?" Two to four options; the page always adds **Not sure**. The card holds the right answer, the lines that show it (`scripts/lib/inbox.mjs:700-705`), those lines quoted word for word, and one sentence why.
- **Assume**, about what you want. "I'm assuming you mean the session you have open, not a headless one." It has no right answer; only you can settle it. You answer Right, Not quite (and say what), or Doesn't matter.
- **Say**, your own words: "Say how you think a review reaches the agent." Step 3.

**Choosing the cards is the point.** A round that tests what you already know wastes your time; a round of trivia is #53 again. So every card carries two lines the agent must write: `likely_wrong:`, why a reasonable person would picture it otherwise (in a repo with no headless command the review does wait, and this one has one), and `matters:`, what depends on it (step 2 of the plan; an agent you didn't expect working on your review). `align` hands the agent four places to look for candidates, and the agent picks the likeliest and costliest:

- **Your words**: what your request takes for granted. "A review that reaches the agent" takes for granted which agent.
- **Your memory**: quick checks you missed on these parts, words you looked up, answers in your own words (`reel memory --you`).
- **What moved**: commits on the pinned files since you last watched a video of these parts.
- **The agent's own assumptions**: what it would have to take for granted to write the plan. These become assume cards.

**The agent's picture is checked too.** A card with a wrong answer would teach you something false. So before you see the predict cards, a fresh agent that never saw this conversation answers each one from the pinned sources alone. Where its answer differs from the card's, the agent's picture is the wrong one: the card is fixed against the code, or dropped. **You never see two answers side by side**, and never a card with a note saying the checker disagreed: a disagreement is settled before the round opens. Who decides, and how: the agent rewrites the card once from the quoted lines, and the checker answers it again. A card reaches you only when the two agree, each reading the quoted lines on its own; neither simply wins, and the checker can misread too, which is why a card that still splits them is dropped rather than shown, and why the lines are on every card for you to read. If they still disagree, the card is dropped and listed at the end of the round as "the agent and the checker read this code differently": a gap between the agent and the code, shown to you, not hidden. The assume cards need no check and come first, so the check runs while you answer them. What a round costs before you see it: the agent's own minute or two to list candidates and write the cards, and one fresh agent reading only the cards and their pinned lines, a few thousand tokens. Step 5 counts it with the rest, so a round's cost can be weighed against the gaps it found.

`align --check` holds a round to its rules before it opens: each quote is in its source word for word (the explainer's `check-sources`), each card has `likely_wrong:` and `matters:`, there are at most six, an assume card has no answer, and no card asks what your memory says you already know, at the same fingerprint.

#### Cases

| Case | Input | What happens | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before a plan | "make Send reach my open session" | Two assume cards, three predict cards on the inbox | you ask: plan; agent lists: candidates; picked: 5 cards; checked: by a fresh agent; you see: the round |
| On its own | `reelplanner align "how a review reaches the agent" scripts/lib/inbox.mjs` | Four predict cards, one say card | you run: align; pinned: inbox.mjs; written: 5 cards; checked: quotes; you see: the round |
| The agent was wrong | A card says Send tries once; the checker reads a second try 15 s later | The card is fixed before you see it | written: card c4; checker answers: tries again; fixed: c4 against the code; you see: the right c4 |
| You know it already | Your memory knows c2 at the same fingerprint | c2 is not asked | listed: c2; memory: known at fingerprint 4b1e; dropped: c2; you see: 4 cards |
| Nothing worth asking | The agent finds no likely, costly gap | No round; the plan says so in a line | agent lists: candidates; none: likely and costly; you see: the plan |

#### Interface

```text
reelplanner align "<topic>" <source> …        # start a round: .reelplanner/align/<date>-<slug>/
  --plan <plan-dir>                          # a round before that plan; its answers go into it
reelplanner align <align-dir> --check         # quotes, likely_wrong, matters, at most six, not known already
reelplanner align <align-dir> --prompt checker  # the fresh agent's exact prompt: answer each predict card from the sources
align.md                                      # your words, then the cards, then (after) what each settled
  ### c1 · predict | assume | say             # one card
  - question:                                 # what you are asked
  - option_a: … option_d:                     # predict only; Not sure is added by the page
  - answer: <letter>                          # predict only
  - source: <path>:<from>-<to>                # predict only, a pinned source
  - quote: "<the lines, word for word>"       # predict only
  - why:                                      # one sentence, shown after you answer
  - likely_wrong:                             # why a reasonable person would picture it otherwise
  - matters:                                  # what depends on it
sources.json                                  # as an explainer's: each source pinned by commit and fingerprint
```

#### Example

You ask for a plan: "make Send reach my open session". Before writing it, the agent lists its candidates and writes five cards. c1, assume: "I'm assuming you mean the session you have open, not a headless run" (`likely_wrong:` your words say "the agent"; `matters:` step 2 of the plan). c3, predict: "In this repo, you press Send and no session is waiting. What happens to the review?" A · it waits in the inbox for the next session, B · a headless run starts on it, C · it is lost. Answer B, from `scripts/lib/inbox.mjs:700-705` and the `agent.command` in `.reelplanner/config.json`. The fresh checker answers B too, so c3 stays. c4 said Send tries once; the checker read the second try 15 seconds later, so c4 is fixed. Your memory knows c5 already, so the round has four cards.

```diagram
flow: How a round is written
your words -> candidates: what they take for granted
your memory --> candidates: missed checks, words looked up
what moved --> candidates: commits since you watched
agent's assumptions -> candidates: assume cards
candidates -> round (at most six): likely and costly | each card says why you might picture it otherwise, and what depends on it
round (at most six) -> fresh checker: predict cards
fresh checker -x round (at most six): a card the code does not back | fixed or dropped before you see it
```

steps.title: One round, three ways to answer it: in the chat, on the page, in a video
steps.text:
**It lets you:** answer a round wherever you already are, in the agent's chat, on the review page or inside a video, and get the same result each way.

Needs step 1's cards. Decided by you as D-314: the round is one **backend** (the record, the checks and where each answer goes) and several ways in. Each way asks the same cards and writes the same answers; it only adjusts how you answer, to what it can do.

**What stays the same everywhere:** the round's folder and `align.md` (step 1), the order (assume cards first, while the checker reads the predict cards), committing to an answer before seeing the code's, and one record of the answers, written by one command, `reelplanner align record <align-dir> <answers.json>`, whichever way they came. Steps 3 and 4 read only that record.

**The three ways in, in the order they are built:**

1. **In the chat, with the agent alone.** No page, no video. The agent asks each card with the harness's own question tool where it has one (`AskUserQuestion` in Claude Code), or as a plain numbered question where it doesn't. You pick, or say Not sure, or write your own words. Then it shows the card's back as text: the file and lines in a code block, the one sentence why. A gap is a second question: Got it, Change the plan, The code is wrong, Show me more. This works in a repo with no `.reelplanner/`: the round is kept in this machine's `~/.reelplanner/align/<repo-key>/`, as a quick video's inbox is, and nothing is written into the repo. This is the one to build first: it needs only the agent. In the chat, a say card is typed (or spoken through the harness's own dictation where it has one), and the session you are talking to is the one that checks it; Show me more answers at once with a longer explanation in text, and the round's one short video, when you asked for it, is built after the round and linked in the chat.
2. **On the review page.** One card at a time, a key per answer, and the card turns over to show the code's lines. Here you can also point (a card whose options are the boxes of a diagram: you click **inbox**) and speak (step 3). **Send** files the round through the inbox as a review is filed, and the waiting session's `--wait` prints it; with no session waiting it stays there, and a round never starts a headless run, as a question asked on the page never does.
3. **In a video.** A quick check is a predict card inside a video, and settles the same way (step 5).

What each way adjusts: the chat has no pointing (a diagram card is asked as its boxes' names) and no voice; the page adds pointing and voice, and later drawing your picture (#23) can come in there, since a drawing needs a page; a video asks only predict cards. On every way:

- **Same picture**: said in a line, and the next card.
- **A gap**: the four ways to settle it (step 4). Nothing goes on until you pick one.
- **Not sure**: kept, never skipped: it is a gap too, of its own kind, because you had no picture of your own. It settles two ways, Got it or Show me more, and the next card comes after.
- **Skip the rest**: ends the round; the cards you skipped go into the plan as **Assumed, not checked**, each in a line.

#### Cases

| Case | Input | What happens | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| In the chat, no `.reelplanner/` | "align me on how a review reaches the agent", in a repo never set up | The agent asks four cards with its question tool | you ask: align me; kept: ~/.reelplanner/align/<repo-key>/; asked: c1 with AskUserQuestion; you pick: B; shown: lines as text |
| Same picture | c3, you press B, the answer is B | ✓ and the next card | you press: B; turned over: lines 700–705; marked: same; next: c4 |
| A gap | c3, you press A | The lines, the why, and the four ways to settle | you press: A; turned over: lines; marked: gap; you see: Got it, Change the plan, The code is wrong, Show me more |
| Not sure | c3, you press N | A gap of its own kind, settled two ways | you press: N; turned over: lines; kept: not sure; you see: Got it, Show me more |
| Pointing, on the page | "Where does a question wait?", a diagram | You click a box | you click: inbox; turned over: lines; marked: same |
| Pointing, in the chat | The same card | Asked as the boxes' names | asked: inbox, a headless run, the session; you pick: inbox |
| Send, no session | All cards answered on the page, nobody waiting | Kept in the inbox, nothing started | you press: Send; saved: inbox; you see: waiting for a session |
| Skipped | Two of five cards answered, then Skip the rest | The plan lists the other three as not checked | you press: Skip the rest; kept: 2 answers; written: plan.md, Assumed, not checked: c3, c4, c5 |

#### Interface

```text
reelplanner align record <align-dir> <answers.json>   # the one record of a round's answers, from any way in
answers.json                                          # [{ card, answer: a | b | … | not-sure | own, own?, settled?, via: chat | page | video }]
chat                                                  # the agent asks each card with its question tool, shows the back as text
reelplanner review <align-dir> --detach               # the page: the round as a row of its own, Round
keys (page)                                           # A–D answer, N Not sure, 1–4 settle a gap, Enter next, S skip the rest
card, front / back (page)                             # the question and options; then the code's lines, the why, your pick and the answer
Send (page)                                           # files the round as inbox/<id>.json, kind: align; never starts a headless run
~/.reelplanner/align/<repo-key>/                      # where a round lives in a repo with no .reelplanner/
```

#### Example

In the chat, in a repo with no `.reelplanner/`, you ask: "align me on how a review reaches the agent before you change it". The agent writes four cards and asks c1 with its question tool: "I'm assuming you mean the session you have open, not a headless run. Right?" You pick Not quite, and say "only my open session". It asks c3: A · it waits for the next session, B · a headless run starts, C · it is lost. You pick A. It shows lines 700 to 702 of `scripts/lib/inbox.mjs` in a code block, and "A headless command is set here, so a review no session picks up starts a headless run." Then: Got it, Change the plan, The code is wrong, Show me more? You pick Got it. `reelplanner align record` writes both answers, and the same round could have been answered on the page instead, card c3 turning over to the same lines.

#### Look

The review page's own look, so a round feels like a part of reviewing, not a new tool: paper `#FAF9F5` and tile `#EFE9DE`, ink `#141413`, and the one coral `#B8552E` only on what is yours (your pick, the settle row while it waits on you). The question in EB Garamond at 44 px, the options and the why in Inter at 22 px, the quoted lines in JetBrains Mono at 20 px on the navy slab `#181715`, as code shows itself everywhere in reelplanner. The one thing that makes it recognisable: the card turns over, front to back, the question on one side and the code's lines on the other, so "you said, the code says" is always one card.

```diagram
flow: One round, three ways in
round (align.md) -> the chat: the agent's question tool | built first; needs no page, no video, no reel init
round (align.md) -> the page: keys, pointing, voice
round (align.md) -> a video: quick checks
the chat -> one record: align record
the page -> one record: Send
a video -> one record: the review
one record -> steps 3 and 4: the same record each way
```

steps.title: Say it in your own words, and see each thing you said checked
steps.text:
**It lets you:** talk through how you think it works for half a minute, and see your own words marked where they match the code and where they don't.

Needs step 2. On the page you can speak; in the chat you type, or use the harness's own dictation where it has one. A say card asks you to explain, not to pick: "Say how you think a review reaches the agent." Hold Space, or press the microphone, and talk. By default the page records on your machine and the local whisper the narration already uses writes your words down when you stop, in a few seconds. A browser's own live recognition shows the words as you speak, but some browsers send the audio to their maker's servers to do it, so it is off until you turn it on, and the switch says so. You can type instead, or fix a word: your words are shown before anything is checked, and nothing is checked until you press **Check**, so a word whisper misheard is fixed first, never marked as a gap. Where there is no microphone, or on a hosted page (which has no local whisper and no session to hand words to), the say card takes typed words only, and says so; where whisper is not installed and live recognition is off, it offers typing and says how to install whisper (`reelplanner setup --local-voice`). The recording stays in the inbox and is never committed; only your words go into `align.md`.

Your words go to the waiting agent session the way a question from Ask about this does: saved first, then handed to a session that is waiting or connected. The agent splits them into **claims**, each one a stretch of your own words that says one thing about the code ("it starts the agent right away"), and checks each against the pinned sources. The page shows your words with each claim marked:

- **✓ matches**, with the lines that back it. The session that marks the claims is the same agent whose picture may be wrong, so each claim it marks is then read by the fresh checker from the quoted lines alone, as a predict card is (step 1), before you see the marks; a claim the two read differently is shown as "not settled", not as a match or a gap;
- **✗ differs**: a gap, made into a card from your own words and the code's lines, settled as in step 4;
- **? the code can't say** (asked next in this same round, and not counted in its six: the limit is on the cards the agent writes, so a full round can become seven): a claim about what you want, not what is. A claim with "should", "I want" or "it'd be better if" is about what should be, so it is **neither a match nor a gap**: the code can only say what is. It becomes an assume card for you to confirm ("I'm assuming you want it to go only to your open session. Right?").

With no session waiting, your words stay with the round in the inbox, and the next session that takes the round checks them; you see them marked when it hands the round back. A say card never starts a headless run, even in a repo that sets a headless command: like a question asked on the page, it waits for a session. In the chat there is always one: the session you are answering is the one that checks your words. So a say card is checked by a session, or not yet; never by a headless run. Until one takes it, the page says "waiting for a session to check your words".

Claims are the shared format: a drawing of your picture (#23) can later produce the same claims, checked the same way.

#### Cases

| Case | Input | What happens | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mostly right | 20 s of speech, 3 claims, 2 match | Two ✓, one ✗ made into a card | you say: 3 things; split: 3 claims; checked: against inbox.mjs; you see: 2 ✓, 1 gap card |
| A want, not a fact | "and it should only go to my session" | A ? claim, as an assume card | you say: should; marked: ?; made: assume card; you answer: Right |
| The default, local | Live recognition off | Recorded, written down by local whisper when you stop | you hold: Space; recorded: 21 s; transcribed: whisper, on this machine; you see: your words |
| Live words, turned on | You switch on the browser's recognition | Words as you speak; the switch says where the audio goes | you turn on: live; you speak: words appear; kept: your words, not the audio |
| No session waiting | Nobody to check | Kept, checked after Send | you say: words; saved: inbox; you see: checked when a session takes the round |

#### Interface

```text
say card                                     # "Say how you think <topic> works"; hold Space or the mic, or type
POST /api/align/say                          # your words, saved under inbox/questions/ before any hand-off
POST /api/align/transcribe                   # a recording, through local whisper, when the browser has no recognition
reelplanner align answer <align-dir> <card> <claims.json>   # the agent's checked claims; the page shows them in seconds
claims.json                                  # [{ words, from, to, verdict: match | differs | open, source, quote }]
  from, to                                   # where in your words the claim is, so the page can mark it
```

#### Example

You hold Space and say: "When I press Send it goes to my session. If I'm not there, it waits for me. A question I ask on the page does the same." Three claims. "It goes to my session": ✓, when a session is waiting (`inbox.mjs:673`). "If I'm not there, it waits": ✗, in this repo a headless run starts, because `config.json` sets `agent.command` (`inbox.mjs:700-705`). "A question does the same": ✓, a question waits and never starts a run (the `!question` on line 700). One gap card appears under your words, with your sentence on its front and the code's lines on its back.

```diagram
flow: Your words, checked
you speak -> your words: browser recognition or whisper
your words -> waiting session: saved first, then handed on
waiting session -> claims: one stretch of your words each
claims -> ✓ matches: the lines that back it
claims -> ✗ differs: a gap card from your words
claims --> ? open: a want, not a fact | becomes an assume card
```

steps.title: Settle each gap, and keep what it settled where it belongs
steps.text:
**It lets you:** close a gap in one click and know it won't come back to bite you, in this plan or a later one.

Needs step 2. A gap is settled one of four ways, each with somewhere to go:

- **Got it**: the code is right and you had it wrong. It goes to your memory (`~/.reelplanner/you.jsonl`) as something you know: the card's claim, its file and lines, and their fingerprint. A later video drops the explanation, the way it already drops a word you know. Decided by you as D-316, it is **asked once more**: the next round on that part, three days or more after you pressed Got it, asks it again on a new case (other names, other numbers, the same rule), never the same card, so you apply what you learned instead of recalling the answer. Got it there too, and it is known for good; wrong again, and it stays a gap to settle. Nothing reminds you on a schedule: the first round in this repo three days or more later, whatever it is about, carries the due card as one more card, so a card you got does come back even when nothing touches that part again; and when a plan starts with cards due and no round is needed, the agent asks them alone, in the chat, a minute at most. If neither ever happens, the card stays due, and `reel memory --you` lists it as due until it is asked. And when those lines change, the fingerprint no longer matches and it counts as not known again, whatever came before. The fingerprint is of the lines' text, not their numbers: when an edit above them moves them, or the file is renamed, the next round finds the same text (in the file, then in the repo) and updates where it is; only when the text itself is gone or changed is it not known, and then the next round that touches it may ask it again, as a new card, never the old one.
- **Change the plan**: you want it your way. Before a plan, it goes into the plan under **You told me first**: the plan is written on it, and its video doesn't ask it again. With no plan, the round's Finish offers **Plan this**, which starts one from the round, as an explainer does; until then your words wait in `align.md` under You told me first, and the plan started from it carries them.
- **The code is wrong**: a fix, never a change made on the spot. Before a plan, it becomes a step of that plan, with the card's lines as its case. With no plan, the round's Finish drafts an issue's text, `align/<slug>/issue.md`, for you to file or to start a plan from. Nothing leaves the machine without you.
- **Show me more**: at once, the card opens a longer explanation and a diagram, from the same pinned lines. At the end of the round, the gaps you asked more on become one short explainer video, built by `reelplanner explain` from the round's sources, which starts from your picture: "You expected the review to wait for you. Here is why a headless run took it." One video for the round, not one a gap: a video takes minutes, a card seconds. It is built in the background at low depth, a few minutes and the tokens of one short video, while you go on, and the plan does not wait for it; the review page says when it is ready, as it does for a rebuilt video.

An assume card answered **Not quite** is a gap about what you want; your words go into the plan as **You told me first**. A card answered **Right** is said in the plan in one line.

**Nothing from a round goes into the decision log.** Only an answer to a plan's question is a decision, and a round is not a plan. What you settle reaches the log through the plan it shapes, as an explainer's comments do. `align.md` keeps the whole record: each card, your answer, same or a gap, and how it was settled. It is committed like an explainer's folder; a recording is never committed.

#### Cases

| Case | Input | What happens | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| Got it | c3, you had A | Known in your memory at its fingerprint, due once more | you press: Got it; kept: you.jsonl, inbox.mjs:700-705 at 4b1e; due: a new case after 3 days |
| Asked once more | A round on the inbox five days later | A new case on the same rule, not c3 again | round: on the inbox; due: c3's rule; asked: a repo with no headless command, what happens?; you pick: it waits; kept: known for good |
| The code changes | Lines 700–705 edited a week later | Not known any more | edited: inbox.mjs; fingerprint: 9c07, not 4b1e; next round: may ask again |
| Change the plan | c1, "Not quite: only my open session" | Into the plan, You told me first | you answer: Not quite; written: plan.md, You told me first; plan video: no question on it |
| The code is wrong | A card's lines do what it says, and you say no code should do that | A step of the next plan, or an issue's text | you press: The code is wrong; drafted: a step; you see: it in the plan |
| Show me more, three gaps | c2, c3, c5 | One explainer at the end of the round | you press: Show me more ×3; made: one explainer; it starts: from what you expected |

#### Interface

```text
Got it                    # you.jsonl: { knows: <claim>, repo, source: path:from-to, fingerprint, due: <date>, asked: 1 }
once more                 # the next round on that part from `due` on asks a new case on the same rule; then known for good
Change the plan           # plan.md, ## You told me first: your words, the card, the code's lines
The code is wrong         # a step of the next plan, or align/<slug>/issue.md for you to file
Show me more              # now: the card's longer page; at the end: one explainer of these gaps
Finish                    # Done · Plan this · Explain the gaps (when any asked for more)
align.md, after           # each card: your answer, same | gap | not sure, how settled
reel memory --you         # lists what you know, by repo, and lets you remove a line
```

#### Example

Of four cards you settle three gaps. c1, "Not quite: only my open session", goes into the plan's You told me first. c3 you had wrong: Got it, kept at fingerprint 4b1e and due once more in three days, on a new case. c4 you asked more on: the card opens the inbox's hand-off order as a diagram (a waiting session, then a connected one, then the headless run, then the inbox), and at Finish, Explain the gaps builds a two-minute explainer that opens with "You expected Send to try once". The plan that follows is written on c1, its video skips what c3 taught you, and nothing went into the decision log.

```diagram
flow: Where a gap goes
gap -> your memory: Got it | asked once more on a new case days later; then known until the lines change
gap -> the plan: Change the plan | You told me first
gap -> a fix: The code is wrong | a step, or an issue's text
gap -> an explainer: Show me more | one video for the round's gaps
gap -x decision log: never directly
```

steps.title: Into the loop: before a plan, in every quick check, and measured
steps.text:
**It lets you:** get a round only when one is worth your time, settle a wrong quick check the same way, and see whether rounds make later surprises rarer.

Needs steps 1 and 4.

**Before a plan.** When you ask for a plan on code that exists, the skill lists gap candidates first (step 1's four places). A candidate is **likely** when one of the four places points at it: your words take it for granted, you missed a check on that part, it changed since you last watched, or it is an assumption the agent can't check alone. It is **costly** when a step of the plan depends on it, or it is hard to undo (stored data and formats, permissions, what other people's code relies on: the walkthrough's own label). You can always ask for one, "align me first", whatever the agent judged. When one is likely and costly, it runs a round before writing the plan, with `--plan` so the answers go into it. The plan then starts from where you stand: what you settled is said in a line, what you knew is not explained again.

**A new project.** With no code yet there is nothing to predict, so a round before a plan in a new project holds only assume and say cards: what the agent assumes you want, and how you picture what you are asking for.

**Every quick check settles like a card.** A quick check is a predict card inside a video. In a plan video, nothing is built yet, so its quick check asks what the plan will do, and settles three ways: Got it (you had the plan wrong), Change the plan, Show me more. A walkthrough's and the system video's quick checks are about code that exists, and add The code is wrong. Today a wrong answer shows Walk me through it and the box "Expected something else?". With this, a wrong answer also offers the same four ways: Got it (into your memory), Change the plan and The code is wrong (each with your words, reaching the agent as a comment does now), Show me more (Walk me through it). The box's words become Change the plan's words, so nothing you can do now is lost. A wrong quick check left unsettled is recorded as it is today, and never blocks Approve.

**Measured.** `reel status` gains a memory line: rounds, gaps found per round, and how they were settled. And it compares later surprises (answers in your own words, "Expected something else", choices you flagged in a walkthrough, late fixes) on plans that had a round with plans that didn't. It reports the counts and says nothing about whether rounds help until five plans of each kind exist. "Each way" means plans that had a round and plans where the agent found a likely, costly gap but no round ran. To compare like with like, the plans without a round it counts are the ones where the agent found a likely, costly gap and no round ran (you skipped it, or rounds were off), not the easy ones where it found none. It prints, for example, `late fixes · with a round 1 · likely gap, no round 4`, and below five plans of each, `too few plans to compare`.

#### Cases

| Case | Input | What happens | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|
| A plan with a likely gap | "make Send reach my open session" | A round of four, then the plan | you ask: plan; candidates: 6; likely and costly: 4; you see: a round, then the plan |
| A plan with none | "rename the Save button" | No round | you ask: plan; candidates: 1, not costly; you see: the plan |
| A wrong quick check | k2, you picked A | The four ways under the answer | you pick: A; you see: B marked, the four ways; you press: Got it; kept: you.jsonl |
| Too early to say | 3 plans with a round, 2 without | Counts only | you run: reel status; you see: 3 rounds, 11 gaps, 7 Got it; "too few plans to compare" |

#### Interface

```text
the plan-to-video skill, A new plan   # lists candidates; runs a round when one is likely and costly
plan.md, ## You told me first         # what the round settled, each with its card
quick check, a wrong answer           # Got it · Change the plan · The code is wrong · Show me more
reel status                           # rounds: 3, gaps: 11 (Got it 7, the plan 3, a fix 1); compared after 5 and 5
```

#### Example

You ask for a plan to make Send reach your open session. The agent finds six candidates, four likely and costly, and opens a round of four. You settle two gaps. The plan is written with "You told me first: only the session you have open". In its video, quick check k2 asks what happens when two sessions are open; you pick A, the wrong one, and press Got it. Three weeks later `reel status` says 3 rounds, 11 gaps, and "too few plans to compare".

```diagram
flow: Before a plan
your request -> candidates: step 1's four places
candidates -> a round: one likely and costly
candidates --> the plan: none worth asking | no round
a round -> the plan: You told me first
the plan -> its video: skips what you knew
```

termMeanings.gap: a place where two of the three pictures of the code disagree: yours, the agent's, or the code itself
termMeanings.round: a short set of cards, at most six, about one topic, that the agent writes where a gap is likely and costly
termMeanings.card: one question in a round: predict, assume or say
termMeanings.predict card: a card that asks what the code does, holding the answer and the code's own lines, quoted
termMeanings.assume card: a card that says what the agent assumes you want, which only you can answer
termMeanings.say card: a card that asks you to explain how you think something works, in your own words
termMeanings.claim: a stretch of your own words that says one thing about the code, checked on its own
termMeanings.fingerprint: a short code worked out from some lines of a file, which changes when one character of them changes
termMeanings.fresh checker: a new agent that never saw this conversation and answers each predict card from the code alone
termMeanings.session: one conversation with your agent, open in a terminal or an app
termMeanings.you told me first: the section of a plan that lists what a round settled, so the plan is written on it and its video doesn't ask it again
termMeanings.got it: settling a gap where the code is right: it goes into your memory as something you know
termMeanings.change the plan: settling a gap where you want it your way: it goes into the plan
termMeanings.the code is wrong: settling a gap as a bug: it becomes a fix
termMeanings.show me more: settling a gap by asking for more: a longer card now, and one short video of the round's gaps at the end
termMeanings.not sure: the answer when you have no picture of your own: a gap of its own kind, settled with Got it or Show me more
termMeanings.skip the rest: ends a round at any time, and the cards you skipped are listed in the plan as not checked
termMeanings.whisper: the speech-to-text program the narration already uses, run on this machine
termMeanings.planned: a picture of what this plan would build: it does not exist yet
termMeanings.pinned: kept as it was when the round was made (the commit, and a fingerprint of each file), so a card quotes only what the code said then
termMeanings.config: the repo's settings file for reelplanner, `.reelplanner/config.json`
termMeanings.askuserquestion: Claude Code's own way for the agent to ask you a multiple-choice question in the chat
termMeanings.draw on a step: mark the step's row with the player's pen, to leave a note on that step
termMeanings.recommended: the option a question's author suggests, marked on its card
